names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Ιουνίου, «Άγιος Ιώβ Μητροπολίτης Μόσχας», with the rank word and the see left off.
The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 1036, «Святитель Иов Московский и всея Руси, патриарх», with the rank words left off.

birth.note: saint.gr: «Γεννήθηκε περί το 1530 μ.Χ. στην Στάριτσα» — the page's own year, with its «περί».

death.note: saint.gr: «κοιμήθηκε το 1607 μ.Χ.», with the page head «(; - 1607)».

feast.note: This day is the synaxis of the hierarchs of Moscow, which the calendar marks «(Моск. Свт.)» and does not expand. His name page lists three other days: «19 июня», his repose, «5 апреля (перенесение мощей)», and «26 января (интронизация)», the day of his enthronement as the first patriarch of Moscow. One row per church is the schema, so the other days are recorded here and he does not render on them.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, 5 октября ст. ст. — «Свтт. Московских Петра, Феогноста, Алексия, Киприана, Фотия, Ионы, Геронтия, Иоасафа, Макария, Филиппа, Иова, Ермогена, Тихона, Петра, Филарета, Иннокентия и Макария.»
source.note: The rank is the alt text of the icon the page sets immediately before this line, «Совершается служба с полиелеем» — a polyeleos service, the one rank on the day above the plain one. He is the eleventh of the seventeen names and the first patriarch on it.

attestations.note: The index keeps his enthronement as a feast in its own right, which for the first patriarch of Moscow is the thing it would keep. It prints no year; the folder's dates still rest on their own source.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιος Ιώβ Μητροπολίτης Μόσχας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. He is none of the corpus's other men of the name — `job-of-pochaev`, `job-of-zographou`, `job-the-hermit-6-march` or `job-the-long-suffering`. The day's line calls him metropolitan of Moscow and the page's own sentence calls him the first patriarch of Moscow, born about 1530 at Staritsa and dead in 1607, with his relics in the Dormition cathedral of the Kremlin; it adds that it has no other details. The page also links a separate commemoration of the translation of his relics, which belongs to another day and is not recorded here. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (1 October 2026).
